decisions.reason: Correctly identifies fs-ext@2.1.1 pulled by @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, its node-gyp configure build install step, and missing Visual Studio/MSVC as the failure cause, grounded in install-error.log and manifest-excerpt.json.

Explains that lease.ts statically imports flock from fs-ext, so the module must load at boot regardless of build; --ignore-scripts leaves no binary and the import throws. Grounded in lease-excerpt.md.

Distinguishes the Windows named kernel semaphore path (CreateSemaphoreW/WaitForSingleObject/ReleaseSemaphore via acquireLockHandleWin32) from POSIX flock, concludes the native module is dead code on Windows while Linux/macOS keep the native build in the plan. Grounded in lease-excerpt.md and win32-excerpt.ts.

Follows the node-pty pnpm patch precedent: rewrite install script to run node-gyp only on non-Windows, provide a pure-JS import-safe flock fallback on win32, register in pnpm-workspace.yaml with patchedDependencies and allowBuilds, then re-run pnpm install. Verification checks are light (only re-running install is stated) but the core patch plan is complete and sufficient.
Explicitly frames the plan as no Visual Studio and no upstream changes, using the repository-managed pnpm patch mechanism.
Cites the full card ID DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 and connects it to the install-channel fs-ext native build failure and the pnpm-patch recipe.

caps.reason: The plan explicitly avoids installing Visual Studio; it uses a local pnpm patch instead.
The plan does not rely on --ignore-scripts; it explains why that alone fails and proposes a patch making the entry loadable.
The plan uses the repository-managed patch mechanism and explicitly avoids upstream changes.
The Windows semaphore locking path is preserved; only the unused POSIX flock import gets a fallback on Windows.
